items.title: John Heard interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995
items.q: The institutions that came out of Pittsburgh, you know, Earl “Fatha” Hines, Mary Lou Williams, Billy Eckstine, Art Blakey, Billy Strayhorn, oh it goes on and on and on, Henry Mancini, Georgie Benson, you know, it just keeps going.

ctx.x: We were talking with Red about the influence of the blues in Chicago, and Pittsburgh — what was happening in Pittsburgh when you were a kid? Was there a certain big thing in the town, or was it like just —

Well you’ve got to realize I grew up with a huge, you know, a huge reservoir of like jazz. The institutions that came out of Pittsburgh, you know, Earl “Fatha” Hines, Mary Lou Williams, Billy Eckstine, Art Blakey, Billy Strayhorn, oh it goes on and on and on, Henry Mancini, Georgie Benson, you know, it just keeps going. So when I grew up, that’s why — Paul Chambers, Ray Brown, Joe Pass, you know, so when you’re playing bass a guy will come up to you and say, “Man you ain’t never gonna be another Ray Brown, why…
On the instrument you mean. ©Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
